chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

My father used to call out in his house, 'al-salat is better than sleep,' and if you were to repeat that, there would be no harm in it. And whatever resembles these two reports among that which includes mention of these expressions, they are to be understood as taqiyyah, due to the consensus of the sect upon leaving action by them; and that is also indicated by...

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Dissimulation or precautionary conformity under particular circumstances.
key_terms.بَأْسٌ: Harm, problem, or objection in a legal sense.
key_terms.بِالصَّلَاةُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ النَّوْمِ: The phrase 'prayer is better than sleep,' mentioned in relation to calling out.
key_terms.تَرْكِ الْعَمَلِ: Abandoning acting upon a report in practice.
key_terms.رَدَّدْتَ: You repeated or echoed the phrase.

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars understand the phrase 'al-salat is better than sleep' in hadith about the adhan?
ai.summary: This report concerns wording connected to the adhan and discusses the phrase 'al-salat is better than sleep.' It indicates that although such wording is reported, reports of this kind are understood under taqiyyah because of the consensus of the Shi'a community not to act upon them in formal practice.
